subject: bfactor() function: "Error: model2 must be an appropriate second-tier model"

messages.author: 67ad43f188b9c5e7
messages.subject: bfactor() function: "Error: model2 must be an appropriate second-tier model"
parts:
Hi Phil,

I tried to replicate your bifactor() codes published in your 2012 paper titled as "mirt: A Multidimensional Item Response Theory Package for the R Environment". 
The codes are exactly the same as yours:

> data("SAT12")
> data <- key2binary(SAT12, key = c(1, 4, 5, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 4, 2, 1, 5, 3, 4, 4, 1, 4, 3, 3, 4, 1, 3, 5, 1, 3, 1, 5, 4, 5))
> specific <- c(2, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 3, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 3, 3, 1, 1, 3, 1, 3, 3, 1, 3, 2, 3, 1, 2)
> guess <- rep(0.1, 32)
> b_mod1 <- bfactor(data, specific, guess)
Error: model2 must be an appropriate second-tier model

But I am not so sure why sometimes I don't have the error and sometimes the error occurred...confused... I am very new to R and mirt.
Your help would be very much appreciated! :) 

Thanks in advance,
Yingyi

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: bfactor() function: "Error: model2 must be an appropriate second-tier model"
parts:
The 2012 paper is now quite dated. You'll have to read the documentation to figure out all the changes (and check the change logs). For this, guess has its own input, and bfactor() now supports two-tier models as well. Use 

b_mod1 <- bfactor(data, specific, guess=guess)

to match the arguments. HTH.

Phil
